text:
jamie: quick sync — I ran a targeted profiler sweep across H100/A100/A10/L4/T4 for the continuous-batching changes. need to lock down max_tokens_per_batch defaults and a short rollout plan. saw a KV-frag regression on H100 when batch token sums crossed ~220k (fallback to slower attention kernel). attaching quick summary below.

jamie: ```profiler summary (sample: 1k synthetic requests, mixed short/long)
GPU   p50_ms  p95_ms  p99_ms  throughput_tps  observed_kv_frag_%  suggested_max_tokens
H100  18      45     78      1200           6.8                 256000
A100  22      60     95      980            5.1                 192000
A10   28      90     140     420            9.4                 96000
L4    32      150    220     210            12.8                48000
T4    40      220    320     150            16.2                40000
```

jamie: notes: H100 gave best throughput but frag spikes -> kernel selector flipped from fused_attn to attn_cuda at ~210–230k tokens; that increased p99 ~+40ms on some traces.

sarah: good data. the kernel fallback is expected when seq*batch crosses block-alignment thresholds; we saw similar on A100 but at higher token sums. for H100 I'd bias toward safety (soft/hard limits). :thumbsup:

mike: agree on soft/hard. propose queue policy: prefer batching up to soft_limit (80% of suggested), start draining after queue_timeout_ms, and avoid forcing KV prefetch for batches above 70% to reduce frag. rough snippet: 

mike: ```json
{
  "policy": "token_budget",
  "soft_fraction": 0.8,
  "hard_fraction": 1.0,
  "queue_timeout_ms": 45,
  "kv_prefetch_for_large": false
}
```

dena: ran a stress run with mixed packing on L4 (10k requests). KV cache fragmentation went +7% vs baseline when hard_max_tokens set to 60k, and p95 jumped ~18%. lowering hard to 48k removed the spike. also saw higher tail for variable-length packing.

jamie: that's consistent with the table. so proposed defaults (for PR): H100=256k, A100=192k, A10=96k, L4=48k, T4=40k, with soft_fraction=0.8 and queue_timeout_ms=50. we'll enable canary in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for 24h.

sarah: we'll also add a kernel-selector telemetry alert if we see >2% fallback rate across any device for 1h. helps catch regressions quickly.

mike: i'll own the rollout script and canary gate. plan: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 3 steps, abort on p99 regress >= 10% or fallback_rate >= 2%.

deploy-bot: canary job queued: batch-presets-v2 -> canary(us-west-2, eu-west-1) 10% traffic. ID: canary-2026-03-20-001.

dena: small extra: add a KV-compact pass after heavy writes (30s window) in the runtime to reduce frag accumulation. I can prototype a cheap compaction that runs at low priority.

jamie: sounds good. i'll open the PR with the defaults + soft/hard + rollout plan + alert thresholds. @mike can you grab the postmortem if the canary trips? @sarah please add the kernel-fallback alert to the dashboard.

mike: yep. will add a short runbook note.

jamie: thanks — aiming to cut the rollout tomorrow morning. if anyone spots an unexpected regression in the canary ping here. :rocket:
